source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And the day of the festival [of the unleavened bread] drew near — the one that is called Passover [Pesach]

translation_notes: וקרב (קרב): Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7128 'hostile encounter', H7130 'center/midst', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because the context is temporal — a day drawing near — making 'approached' the natural reading.

פ!סח (פסח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over', H6453 'Passover (the festival or victim)', H6454 'Paseach (name)', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because it is explicitly named as the festival being described.
textual_notes: The consonants ש! and פ!סח contain damage markers (!). The ש! likely represents the relative particle שׁ (that/which). The פ! likely preserves פ as the initial letter of פסח.

verses.literal: And approached [the] day [of the] festival [of the unleavened bread] that is called Passover

verses.translation: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking [searching for] how they might put him to death, but they feared the people

translation_notes: ושרי (שרי): Candidates: H8297 'Sarai', H8298 'Sharay'. Neither fits; the consonants שׂר (prince/chief) with the plural construct ending ־י are contextually obvious — these are 'chiefs of' (as in שָׂרֵי). The Strong's candidates listed share consonants but the root is שׂר H8269.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because it functions as a limiting conjunction — they wanted to kill him BUT feared the people.
העם (עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because the article ה prefixed indicates a noun 'the people', not the preposition 'with'.
textual_notes: The consonants הכה״נים and לה״מיתו contain quotation marks (״) indicating abbreviation or textual notation. הכה״נים is clearly הכהנים 'the priests'. לה״מיתו is the hiphil infinitive construct of מות with 3ms suffix — 'to cause him to die / to put him to death'.

verses.literal: And [the] chiefs [of] the priests and the scribes [were] searching how they could put him to death but [were] fearing the people

verses.translation: And the Adversary [Satan] entered into Yuda, the one called Ish Qeriyot [man of Kerioth], one of the twelve. And Pilate asked him, Are you [the] king of the Jews? And he answered him, You [yourself] say [it].

translation_notes: והשטן (שטן): Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'an opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because the article ה is prefixed making it a noun — 'the adversary/Satan' — and the context describes an entity entering a person.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to act manly'. Chose H376 because it forms the epithet 'man of Kerioth' — a place-name designation.

מה: Used here as an abbreviation or contraction in the compound number — the text reads מה נים עשר meaning 'from the two-ten' = 'from the twelve'. The מ likely serves as the preposition 'from' and the ה as article, yielding 'from the'.
עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6240 '-teen (in combination)'. Chose H6240 because this is a compound number — שנים עשר = twelve.
מלך: Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 because the syntax requires a noun — 'king of the Jews'.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because Yeshua is responding to a question directed at him — 'you say [it]'.
שואל: The root שאל (H7592 'to inquire') is present here in participial form. The candidates listed under אל are fragments; the full word is a participle of שאל.
textual_notes: א!חד contains a damage marker (!). The word is likely אחד 'one'.
נים appears to be the remnant of שנים (two), with the initial שׁ possibly absorbed into the preceding word or lost. The compound מה נים עשר = 'from the twelve'.

אתהו could be parsed as אתה + הוא (you [are] he) or as את + suffix (a sign/mark of him). Context of the question 'are you the king' supports reading it as 'you [are] he' — an interrogative construction.
אומר lacks a Strong's entry for the verb form; H201 'Omar' is a proper name. The word here is clearly the active participle of אמר (H559) — 'saying/say'.

verses.literal: And the adversary entered into Yuda the one called man [of] Qeriyot one from the two [and] ten And Pilat asks him [are] you king [of] the Yehudim and he answered him you say

verses.translation: He went and spoke with the chief priests and the rabbis [about] in what way [on which side] he could hand over [betray] Yeshua to them. And Pilate said to the chief priests and to the soldiers, I find no cause [reason, charge] in this man that he should die.

translation_notes: ודבר (דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the vav-consecutive + verb form fits narrative sequence — 'and he spoke'.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because the syntax requires a preposition — he spoke WITH the chief priests.
שרי: Same as section 2 — construct plural of שׂר 'chief/prince' (H8269), not the proper names listed.

באי (אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because with the prefix ב it forms 'in which/how' — introducing the question of what method to use for betrayal.
ז!ה: Damage marker; reading as זה H2088 'this' — combined with באי צד yields 'in which side/way'.
צד: Candidates: H6654 'a side', H6655 'at the side of'. Chose H6654 — 'side' used figuratively as 'way/manner', asking on which side/in what way he could betray him.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the form is a completed verb — 'said'.
בזה: The ב prefix + זה (H2088) 'in this'. Candidates H959 'to disesteem' and H961 'booty' don't fit — the context requires 'in this [man]'.
האדם (אדם): Candidates: H119 'flush', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 because with the article it means 'the man' — referring to the accused person.
שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/set', H7762 'garlic'. Chose H7760 used in late Hebrew as 'any/some' (שום = no sort of, any kind of).
טעם: Candidates: H2938 'to taste', H2940 'perception/judgment/reason', H2942 'judgment/account'. Chose H2940 because as a noun it means 'reason/cause/charge' — Pilate finds no reason for execution.
textual_notes: ש!הלך and ז!ה and לה!ם contain damage markers. ש!הלך is likely שׁהלך (that he went). לה!ם is likely להם (to them).
מוצא is listed as H4161 'a going forth/source' but in context this is the active participle of מצא (H4672 'to find') — 'I am not finding'. The participial form מוצא from מצא fits perfectly.
The text appears to combine two narrative threads — Judas's betrayal negotiation and Pilate's verdict — which may represent a condensed or composite manuscript.

verses.literal: That he went and spoke with [the] chiefs [of] the priests and the rabbis in which side he would hand over to them Yeshua And Pilat said to [the] chiefs [of] the priests and to the soldiers I am not finding in this the man any reason [that] he should die

verses.translation: And they rejoiced and promised [vowed] him silver [money]. And they were crying out and saying, He causes the people to be turned away [overturned], teaching in all Judah, from the Galilee region and as far as here.

translation_notes: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the vav-prefix + pronoun 'and they' introduces the next clause about the accusers crying out.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — the independent pronoun 'he' as subject of the accusation.
באופן (אופן): H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew, אופן develops the meaning 'manner/way' (cf. modern Hebrew). The context requires 'in [a] manner/way' — he acts in such a way that the people are turned.
שהעם (עם): Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 — the relative שׁ + article ה + עם = 'that the people'.
לאחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H312 'another/other'. Chose H312 'another/other' — the people are turned to another [way/teaching].
מלמד: Candidates: H4451 'a goad', H3925 'to teach'. Chose H3925 because the piel participle 'teaching' fits — he is teaching throughout all Judah. H4451 'goad' would be a forced image here.
בכל (כל): Candidates: H3605 'all/whole'. Straightforward — 'in all [of]'.
עד: Candidates: H5703 'terminus/perpetuity', H5704 'as far as/until', H5707 'witness'. Chose H5704 — spatial extent, 'as far as here'.
כאן (אן): H575 'where/whither/hither'. With כ prefix, this yields 'like here' or simply 'here' in later Hebrew usage.
כסף: Candidates: H3700 'to pine after/desire', H3701 'silver/money'. Chose H3701 — they promised him money. The word is split across two tokens (כ!ס! and ף) due to manuscript damage.
textual_notes: כ!ס!ף is split across two tokens with damage markers, but clearly represents כסף 'silver/money'.
The phrase באופן שהעם נהפך לאחר uses late/medieval Hebrew syntax. באופן functions as 'in such a way that', which is post-biblical usage.
מלמד could be parsed as either a noun 'teacher/goad' or a piel participle 'teaching'. The participial reading 'teaching' better fits the accusation that he teaches throughout Judah.

verses.literal: And they rejoiced and vowed to him silver And they [are] crying out and saying he makes in [a] manner that the people turns to another teaching in all Yehudah from Galilah and unto here

verses.translation: And he promised [vowed] to them — [he was] standing, standing here. And the winepress drew near, and the Passover drew near. And when Pilate heard [the word] Galilee, he asked concerning the man whether he was a Galilean.

translation_notes: והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — independent pronoun 'and he' as subject.
ויקב (יקב): H3342 'a wine-vat/trough'. This is puzzling in context. It may be a scribal error or a fragment. The text seems disrupted here.
קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7128 'hostile encounter', H7130 'center', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 — 'approached/drew near', continuing the temporal narrative about Passover approaching.
פסח: Candidates: H6452 'to skip over', H6453 'Passover', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 — the Passover festival, consistent with section 1.
וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H834 'who/which/when', H833 'to be straight'. Chose H834 — the conjunction וכאשר means 'and when'.
שמע: Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8088 'a report'. Chose H8085 — completed verb 'heard'.
שאל: Candidates: H7592 'to inquire', H7594 'Sheal'. Chose H7592 — 'he asked/inquired'.
האדם: Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 — 'the man', referring to the accused.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — introduces an indirect question: whether he was a Galilean.
הוא: H1931 'he' — pronoun in the indirect question.

גללי: H1562 'Gilalai'. The consonants גללי here likely represent 'Galilean' (a gentillic adjective from גליל), though the Strong's entry is for a personal name. In context this clearly means 'a Galilean'.
textual_notes: The text in this section appears disrupted. The sequence 'ויקב קרב ויקרב י פסח' is confused — it seems to contain duplications or scribal errors. ויקב could be a corruption of ויקרב (and approached), with the subsequent קרב being a duplicate. The isolated י may be a fragment.
The phrase 'עומד עומד כאן' with the double 'standing' is unusual — possibly emphatic repetition or a scribal dittography.
The section seems to conflate material from different narrative moments — the vow/promise (from the betrayal scene) and the Pilate/Galilee inquiry.

verses.literal: And he promised to them standing standing here and [the] winepress approached and approached the Passover And when Pilat heard Galilah he asked him the man if he [is] a Galilean

verses.translation: And the day arrived when they make unleavened bread [matzot] — on that [very] day it was necessary [or: compelled] that he would die at [the time of] the Passover

translation_notes: לחם (ל-ח-ם): Candidates: H3898 'to feed on/consume/battle', H3899 'food/bread/grain', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because the context specifies a type of bread — 'bread of unleavened-bread' is a standard phrase for matzot.

מצות: The provided candidate H4695 'a quarrel' does not fit. The consonants מ-צ-ו-ת also match H4682 (unleavened bread/matzot), which is the standard term for the unleavened bread of Passover. H6702 'to blaze' also does not fit.
היה (ה-י-ה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because the sentence requires a copula — 'it was compelled.'

בפסח (פ-ס-ח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over', H6453 'Passover', H6454 'Paseach (name)', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because the context is about the day of unleavened bread, which is the Passover festival.
textual_notes: מצות — The Strong's system provided H4695 'quarrel' and H6702 'to blaze', neither of which fits. The reading is almost certainly מצות (matzot, H4682), unleavened bread, which was not listed among the candidates but is the only contextually coherent reading.
שימות — parsed as ש + ימות (that he would die). This is a striking theological statement: the text says it was 'compelled/necessary' that he die at Passover time.
מוכרח — a later Hebrew form meaning 'forced/compelled/necessary.' No Strong's candidates provided.

verses.literal: And came the day that they make bread [of] unleavened-bread in that day it was compelled that he would die at the Passover

verses.translation: And he sent Kefa [Peter] and Yochanan [John], saying: Go and prepare the Passover [meal] so that we may eat [it]

translation_notes: ושלח (ש-ל-ח): Candidates: H7971 'to send away/for/out', H7972 'to send (Aramaic)', H7973 'spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)', H7975 'Shiloach (fountain)'. Chose H7971 because the context requires a verb of dispatching — he sent two people on a mission.
הפסח (פ-ס-ח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over', H6453 'Passover', H6454 'Paseach', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because the instruction is to prepare the Passover meal.
לכו: The provided candidate H3551 'window' for כו does not apply. לכו is the imperative plural of הלך (to go, H1980) — 'go!'
textual_notes: כיפא — Aramaic name meaning 'rock/stone.' No Strong's candidates provided. This is the Aramaic equivalent of Peter.
אומר — Strong's only offers H201 'Omar (name)', but this is clearly a participle of אמר (H559) — 'saying.'

verses.literal: And he sent Kefa and Yochanan saying go and prepare the Passover that we eat

verses.translation: And they said: To where [or: where] do you desire [or: wish] that we prepare it?

translation_notes: והם (ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because the context requires a pronoun — the disciples are responding.
אתה (א-ת-ה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence is a question directed at the speaker — 'where do you desire?'
חפץ (ח-פ-ץ): Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/be pleased with', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. Chose H2654 because the context requires a verb — 'do you desire/wish?'
textual_notes: שנכינהו — parsed as ש + נכין + הו (that we prepare it). The suffix הו is a 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun referring to the Passover meal.

verses.literal: And they said to where you desire that we prepare it

verses.translation: And he said to them: Behold, when you enter into the city you will meet a certain man carrying a vessel [or: jar, jug] of water — follow [go after] him into the house that he enters

translation_notes: והוא (ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because the context needs a pronoun subject — 'and he said.'
אמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 (various). Chose H559 — the standard verb of speech in a narrative context.
להם (ה-ם): The candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit. Reading as preposition ל + pronoun הם (H1992 'them') — 'to them.'
הנה (ה-נ-ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because it introduces a visual instruction — 'behold, when you enter...'

בעיר (ע-י-ר): Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass'. Chose H5892 because the narrative describes entering an urban setting to find a house.

אדם (א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because the context describes encountering a person — 'a man carrying water.'
אחד (א-ח-ד): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one man' meaning 'a certain man.'
של (ש-ל): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of/of'. Chose H7945 because it functions as the possessive/genitive particle — 'of water.'

מים (מ-י-ם): Candidates: H4325 'water', H3220 'sea', H3221 'sea (Aramaic)', H3222 'warm spring'. Chose H4325 because a man carrying a vessel of water is the natural reading — a sea or warm spring makes no sense as something carried.
בבית (ב-י-ת): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'object marker'. Chose H1004 because the instruction is to follow the man into the house he enters.
textual_notes: א*שישה — This word has a damaged/marked letter (the asterisk on the shin). It could be אשישה from H809 (a raisin cake/pressed cake), but in this context a container for carrying water is needed. It may be a variant or dialectal form for a jar/vessel/jug. The reading 'vessel/jar' fits the physical image of a man carrying water.
כא*שר — reading as כאשר 'when/as', with the asterisk marking a damaged letter.
אח*ריו — reading as אחריו 'after him', with the asterisk on a damaged letter.

verses.literal: And he said to them behold when you come in the city you will meet a man one carrying a vessel of water go after him into the house that he enters

verses.translation: And you shall say to the master [or: owner] of the house: The Lord [or: Master] says to you — where is the place where he will eat the Passover with his disciples?

translation_notes: לבעל (ב-ע-ל): Candidates: H1166 'to be master/marry', H1167 'master/owner/husband', H1168 'Baal (deity)', H1169 'master'. Chose H1167 because 'master/owner of the house' is a standard idiom for the householder.
הבית (ב-י-ת): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith'. Chose H1004 — the standard Hebrew word for house.
האדון (א-ד-ו-ן): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because the context is a title — 'the Lord/Master says to you.'
הוא (ה-ו-א): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as a copular pronoun — 'where is the place.'
המקום (מ-ק-ו-ם): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise', H6966 'to rise (Aramaic)'. Chose H4725 because the question asks about a location — 'the place where he will eat.'
הפסח (פ-ס-ח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop over', H6453 'Passover', H6454 'Paseach', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 — the Passover meal.
עם (ע-ם): Candidates: H5971 'people/tribe', H5972 'people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5973 because the preposition 'with his disciples' is the natural reading.

אנה (א-נ-ה): Candidates: H578 'to groan', H579 'to approach/meet'. Neither fits perfectly; however, אנה also functions as an interrogative adverb 'where?' (related to H575 אן). Chose this reading because the sentence is a question about location.
textual_notes: אנה — The provided candidates H578 'groan' and H579 'approach' do not fit the interrogative context. Reading as the interrogative 'where?' (related to אן, H575), which shares consonants and is well attested in biblical Hebrew.
אומר — Again, the only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar', but this is clearly a participle of H559 — 'says/is saying.'

verses.literal: And you will say to the master of the house the lord says to you where is the place that he will eat the Passover with his disciples

verses.translation: And he will show you a large [or: great] hall [or: upper room, palace chamber], and there you shall prepare it

translation_notes: היכל (ה-י-כ-ל): Candidates: H1964 'a large public building/palace/temple', H1965 'same (Aramaic)', H3201 'to be able', H3202 'to be able (Aramaic)'. Chose H1964 because the context describes a room/hall for a Passover meal — a large public building or grand room.
גדול (ג-ד-ו-ל): Only candidate H1419 'great'. Straightforward — modifies the hall as 'great/large.'
ושם (ש-ם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/honor', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 because the sentence gives a location instruction — 'and there you will prepare.'
textual_notes: ירא*ך — reading as יראך 'he will show you,' from ראה in the hiphil (causative) stem — 'he will cause you to see / show you.' The asterisk marks a damaged letter.
היכל — typically refers to a temple or palace hall. In this domestic context it likely means a large upper room or banquet hall, not necessarily a temple.

verses.literal: And he will show you a hall great and there you will prepare it

verses.translation: And the disciples went, and when the circumstances [or: assistance, things needed] came to them, they found [everything] just as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover

translation_notes: להם (first and second): Candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit. Reading as preposition ל + pronoun הם (H1992) — 'to them.'
שאמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 (various). Chose H559 — 'that he said.'
הפסח (פ-ס-ח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop over', H6453 'Passover', H6454 'Paseach', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 — the Passover meal preparation.
textual_notes: וכלכת — This appears to be a form meaning 'and the going of' or 'and when... went.' Could be related to הלך (to go) or כלך. The form is unusual and may reflect a later Hebrew dialectal construction.

הסייעות — 'the helps/assistances.' This is from the root סיע (to help/assist), in feminine plural form. It likely means 'the things needed' or 'the favorable circumstances/assistance.' No Strong's candidates provided.
שיבואו — parsed as ש + יבואו (when they came / when [things] came). The subject could be 'the helps/circumstances' — i.e., when the needed things materialized for them.

verses.literal: And the going of the disciples when came the helps to them they found as that he said to them and they prepared the Passover

verses.translation: And when the appointed hour arrived, they reclined to eat, and the twelve emissaries [or: sent-ones, apostles] [were] with him

translation_notes: עשר (consonants ע.ש.ר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'ten in combination (-teen)'. Chose H6240 because it follows שנים (two), forming 'two-ten' = twelve, a standard Hebrew compound numeral.
textual_notes: ה<עה and ה<לוחים contain a character (<) that likely represents a damaged or uncertain letter in the manuscript. From context, ה<עה is almost certainly השעה (the hour) and ה<לוחים is השלוחים (the sent-ones/emissaries). The < may represent a shin (ש) or similar consonant lost to manuscript damage.

verses.literal: And when the hour arrived they sat to eat and twelve the sent-ones [were] with him

verses.translation: And he said, With deep longing [or: yearning desire] I eat with you this Passover before I endure the death

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א.מ.ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the verb 'and he said' is the natural reading introducing direct speech.

זה (consonants ז.ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this' is the demonstrative modifying 'the Passover' — 'a sheep the Passover' would be redundant and awkward.

פסח (consonants פ.ס.ח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over/spare', H6453 'Passover (the festival or the sacrifice)', H6454 'Paseach (name)', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because preceded by the article ה and the demonstrative זה, indicating the festival/meal being eaten.
textual_notes: בכוסף appears to be a late/medieval Hebrew form (ב + כוסף/כיסופין = with longing/yearning). This is not a standard biblical Hebrew word but is well attested in post-biblical Hebrew. The consonants כסף could also relate to H3701 'silver' or H3700 'to long for/yearn', but the form with ו suggests the noun 'longing/desire' from the root כסף.
שאסבול is a compound: ש (that/which) + א (first person prefix) + סבול (suffer/bear), from the root סבל. This is post-biblical Hebrew morphology.
המיתה is ה + מיתה (death), a late Hebrew nominal form from the root מות.

verses.literal: And he said with longing I eat with you this the Passover before that I suffer the death

verses.translation: For I say to you that I will not eat it until [the] kingdom [or: dominion, reign] of YHWH is fulfilled [or: completed, brought to fullness]

translation_notes: כי (consonants כ.י): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal/explanatory clause following the prior statement.
אני (consonants א.נ.י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the speaker is self-referencing, and 'a ship saying to you' produces no coherent image.

אומר: The only Strong's candidate listed is H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants א.מ.ר are clearly the participle of H559 'to say'. The form אומר is the active qal participle 'saying/one who says'. Assigning H559 in participial form.

עד (consonants ע.ד): Candidates: H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because 'until that it will be completed' is the natural temporal conjunction.
מלכות (consonants מ.ל.כ.ו.ת): Candidates: H4438 'a rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah'. Chose H4438 because 'kingdom of YHWH' forms a coherent theological phrase, whereas 'Cuthah of YHWH' does not.
יהוה (consonants י.ה.ו.ה): Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH'. Both refer to the same divine name. Chose H3068 as the primary entry.
textual_notes: שיהא is a post-biblical Hebrew form: ש (that) + יהא (will be), from the root הוה/היה. This is a common Mishnaic/Talmudic construction.

נשלם could be parsed as nifal passive participle 'completed/fulfilled' from שלם, or as a nifal perfect. Context (following שיהא 'will be') favors the passive participle: 'until the kingdom of YHWH will be completed/fulfilled.'

verses.literal: For I saying to you that-not I will eat it until that will be completed [the] kingdom of YHWH

verses.translation: And when he took the cup, he offered supplication [or: gave thanks, blessed], and said, Take it and divide it among yourselves

translation_notes: אשר (consonants א.ש.ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר = 'and when', introducing a temporal clause — the most natural reading before an action verb.
לקח (consonants ל.ק.ח): Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction received'. Chose H3947 because the physical action of taking a cup is coherent; 'he instructed the cup' is not.

חנות (consonants ח.נ.ו.ת): Candidates: H2588 'a vault/cell/prison', H2589 'supplication'. Chose H2589 because 'he made supplication' (עשה חנות) describes a prayer/blessing over the cup, which is contextually natural at a Passover meal. 'He made a prison' with a cup makes no sense.
אמר (consonants א.מ.ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564 various. Chose H559 because it introduces the direct speech command that follows.
textual_notes: חנות as H2589 'supplication' likely renders a thanksgiving blessing or prayer. This Hebrew word choice may be translating a concept of 'giving thanks/blessing' using the root חנן (grace/supplication). This is a significant interpretive choice — the text says he 'made supplication' rather than 'gave thanks' or 'blessed.'

verses.literal: And when he took the cup he made supplication and said take it and divide it among yourselves

verses.translation: For I say to you that I will not drink again from what comes forth [or: the produce] of the vine until [the] kingdom [or: reign] of YHWH comes

translation_notes: כי: Same as section 3. Chose H3588 as conjunction 'for/because'.
אני: Same as section 3. Chose H589 'I'.

עוד (consonants ע.ו.ד): Candidates: H5749 'to duplicate/repeat/testify', H5750 'again/still/more', H5751 same (Aramaic). Chose H5750 because 'I will not drink again' is a natural adverbial use; 'I will not drink testimony' or 'I will not drink testify' makes no sense.
עד: Same as section 3. Chose H5704 'until'.
מלכות: Chose H4438 'kingdom/dominion' as in section 3.
יהוה: Chose H3068 as in section 3.
textual_notes: מהיוצא is מ (from) + ה (the) + יוצא (going out / what comes forth), a participle from יצא (to go out). This phrase 'from what goes forth from the vine' is a circumlocution for wine or the fruit/produce of the vine.
שיבא is ש (that/until) + יבא (he/it will come), from the root בוא. The subject is מלכות יהוה — 'until the kingdom of YHWH comes.'

verses.literal: For I saying to you that-not I will drink again from-the-going-out from-the-vine until that comes [the] kingdom of YHWH

verses.translation: And he took the bread [or: morsel] and offered supplication [or: gave thanks], and broke it and gave it to them, saying: This is my body, the [one] given on your behalf — this you shall do for my remembrance [or: as my memorial]

translation_notes: לקח: Chose H3947 'to take' as in section 4.

פת (consonants פ.ת): Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel (of bread)', H6596 'a hole/hinge/pudenda'. Chose H6595 because taking bread at a meal produces a coherent image; 'he took the hole/hinge' does not.
חנות: Chose H2589 'supplication' as in section 4, describing a prayer/blessing over the bread.

להם: The preposition ל + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because 'and gave it to them' is the natural reading — he distributed bread to the people with him.
זה (first instance): Chose H2088 'this' as the demonstrative pronoun in 'this is my body.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it/is', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the copula 'is' in 'this is my body.'
זה (second instance): Chose H2088 'this' as demonstrative referring to the act just described.
textual_notes: גופי is גוף + י (my body). The word גוף is not a standard biblical Hebrew word (biblical Hebrew uses בשר for 'flesh/body'). גוף for 'body' is post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew, consistent with the late linguistic register of this manuscript.
הנתון is the passive participle of נתן (to give) with the article: 'the given [one]' — i.e., 'which is given.'
ובצעו: ו + בצע + ו (and-he-broke-it), from the root בצע 'to break/cut off (bread).' The suffix ו is the 3ms object pronoun 'it.'

verses.literal: And he took the bread and made supplication and broke-it and gave-it to them saying this is my body the given on-behalf-of-you this you-will-do for-my-remembrance

verses.translation: And likewise the goblet — and when they had eaten, he said: This goblet is my covenant-command [or: commandment], the new [one], in my blood — that which will be poured out on your behalf

translation_notes: כן (consonants כ.ן): Candidates: H3651 'so/likewise/thus', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and likewise the goblet' naturally continues from the bread action — 'and a gnat the goblet' or 'and a pedestal the goblet' produces no coherent image.
אשר in וכאשר: Chose H834 'when' as temporal conjunction, same reasoning as section 4.
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — introducing direct speech.
זה: Chose H2088 'this' as demonstrative modifying 'the goblet.'
הוא: Chose H1931 as copula 'is' — 'this goblet is my commandment.'

חדש (consonants ח.ד.ש): Candidates: H2318 'to be new/rebuild', H2319 'new', H2320 'new moon/month', H2321 'Chodesh (name)'. Chose H2319 because 'the new' modifies the commandment/covenant — 'the new moon in my blood' is less coherent.

דמי: The listed candidate is H1824 'quiet'. However, בדמי in this context almost certainly derives from דם (H1818, 'blood') with the 1cs possessive suffix י — 'in my blood.' The consonants ד.מ.י match both readings. 'In my blood' makes immediate physical and ritual sense with a cup and pouring out; 'in my quiet' does not.
textual_notes: צווי appears to be צוו + י (my commandment), from the root צוה (to command). This is unusual — most traditions render this concept as 'covenant' (ברית). The Hebrew manuscript distinctly uses a word from the root צוה, meaning 'command/commandment/ordinance.' This may reflect a deliberate theological choice or a different textual tradition. The reading 'my commandment, the new [one]' is internally consistent.

בדמי: The Strong's candidate listed is H1824 'quiet' (דמי). However, the consonants ד.מ.י can equally represent דם + י (my blood, from H1818). Given the context of a cup, pouring out, and on behalf of others, 'in my blood' is overwhelmingly the coherent reading. I assign this to H1818 + 1cs suffix rather than H1824.
נשפך is the nifal participle or perfect of שפך (to pour out) — 'poured out' or 'being poured out.'

verses.literal: And likewise the goblet and when they ate he said this the goblet it [is] my commandment the new in-my-blood that which will be poured-out on-behalf-of-you

verses.translation: Yet surely, behold — the hand of the one who delivers me [or: hands me over, betrays me] is [here] on the table

translation_notes: הנה (consonants ה.נ.ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'surely behold, the hand...' is a natural attention-drawing interjection; 'surely themselves, the hand...' or 'surely lamentation, the hand...' do not fit.

יד (consonants י.ד): Candidates: H3027 'a hand (indicating power, direction)', H3028 same (Aramaic). Chose H3027 because this is a Hebrew text — the hand of the betrayer is physically present at the table.

מוסר (consonants מ.ו.ס.ר): Candidates: H4147 'chastisement/halter/restraint', H4148 'chastisement/reproof/warning/instruction/restraint'. Both derive from the root יסר. However, in context, המוסר אותי should be understood as a participle from מסר (to hand over/deliver up/betray), a common post-biblical Hebrew verb. The manuscript uses this form to mean 'the one handing me over.' This is consistent with the post-biblical register of the text.
textual_notes: המוסר: The Strong's candidates point to מוסר from יסר (discipline/chastisement). However, in post-biblical Hebrew, מוסר from the root מסר means 'one who hands over/delivers/betrays.' The participial form המוסר אותי = 'the one delivering me up.' This is the reading that makes contextual sense — a hand belonging to a betrayer at the table. The biblical Hebrew reading 'the discipliner of me' is possible but far less coherent in this narrative.
ב<ולחן: The < likely represents a damaged letter, almost certainly ש, yielding בשולחן (on/at the table). The word שולחן (table, H7979) is standard biblical Hebrew.

verses.literal: Surely behold [the] hand of the one-delivering me she [is] on-the-table

verses.translation: And in truth, the son of humanity [or: the human one] is indeed going according to what [is determined], but surely — woe to that one who will betray me

translation_notes: אמת (consonants א.מ.ת): Only candidate H571 'stability/truth/trustworthiness'. Clear reading.
בן (consonants ב.ן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of the human' is a title/designation, not a proper name.

אדם (consonants א.ד.ם): Candidates: H119 'to turn rosy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (name/place)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. Chose H120 because 'son of the human' (בן האדם) is a well-known designation meaning 'human one/mortal' — 'son of Edom' or 'son of Adam the place' would be unexpected and contextually unjustified.
הוא in שהוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because ש + הוא = 'that he [is]' — a relative clause.

אפס (consonants א.פ.ס): Candidates: H656 'to disappear/cease', H657 'cessation/end; adverbially: no further, however, but'. Chose H657 in its adverbial sense 'indeed/certainly' — 'the son of the human is indeed going' describes a determined departure. 'The son of the human disappears going' is less natural.

אוי (consonants א.ו.י): Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation/Oh!', H189 'Evi (a Midianite chief)'. Chose H188 because 'woe to that one' is a natural exclamation of judgment; a proper name here is nonsensical.
textual_notes: כפי is כ + פי (according to / as per), literally 'as the mouth of' — a common Hebrew idiom meaning 'according to what.' This suggests the son of the human goes according to what has been determined/appointed.

שהוא אפס הולך: The syntax is ambiguous. It could read 'according to what he indeed goes' (i.e., according to what is determined, he is going) or 'according to what he is, he certainly goes.' The overall sense is the same: his departure/death is predetermined.
שיבגוד is ש + י + בגד (who will betray/deal treacherously), from the root בגד (H898, to deal treacherously/betray). The form with ו in the middle may reflect a post-biblical conjugation pattern.

verses.literal: And in truth [the] son of the human according-to what he [is] indeed going but surely woe to that-one who will betray me

verses.translation: And they began to question among themselves which one of them [it was] who would do this

translation_notes: הם in והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'and they began to ask' is the natural subject; 'and wealth began' or 'and Ham began' is not contextually coherent.

לשאול: The Strong's candidates listed are H7585 'Sheol/Hades', H7586 'Shaul (name)', H193 'the body/powerful'. However, these consonants ש.א.ל clearly represent the infinitive of שאל (H7592, to ask/inquire). 'To ask among themselves' is the coherent reading; 'to Sheol among themselves' or 'to Saul among themselves' makes no narrative sense.
הם in מהם: Chose H1992 'them' — 'from among them.'
זה in שזה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'who would do this' is coherent; 'who would do a sheep' is not.
textual_notes: איזהו is a compound: אי (which) + זה (this) + הוא (he) = 'which one is he' — a standard post-biblical Hebrew interrogative meaning 'which one.' This confirms the late linguistic register of the manuscript.
יעשה could be parsed as imperfect (would do / will do) from עשה (H6213). The imperfect here conveys potential/future action: 'who would do this.'

verses.literal: And they began to ask among-themselves which-one from-them that this would do

verses.translation: And there arose a dispute [or: contention, division] between

translation_notes: והיה (consonants והיה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become/come to pass', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 because 'and it came to be' naturally introduces a narrative event — a dispute arising — whereas 'ruin' or the divine name make no sense before 'dispute between'.

בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand/distinguish', H996 'between', H997 'between'. Chose H996 because 'between' is the expected preposition following 'dispute' — 'a dispute between [parties]'.
textual_notes: מחלוקת has no Strong's candidates listed; it is a noun from the root חלק (to divide) meaning 'dispute/division/controversy'. No Strong's number assigned in the provided data.

verses.literal: And there was a dispute between

verses.translation: Kings of the nations rule [or: exercise lordship] over them, and those who have dominion [or: authority] over them are called luminaries [or: benefactors] of covenant

translation_notes: בהם (consonants בהם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because ב + הם = 'over/in them', which fits 'kings rule over them'.
ובין (consonants ובין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between', H997 'between'. Chose H996; the conjunction ו + בין continues the comparison — 'and among/between those who...'.

אשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because it serves as the relative pronoun introducing 'those who have dominion'.
להם (consonants להם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as ל + הם = 'to them', indicating possession — 'those who have authority to them (i.e., over them)'.
ממשלה (consonants ממשלה): Candidates: H4475 'rule/dominion', H7951 'to be tranquil', H7952 'to mislead', etc. Chose H4475 because 'dominion/rule' fits the context of kings exercising authority.

ברית (consonants ברית): Candidates: H1285 'a compact/covenant', H1286 'Berith (deity)', H1287 'vegetable alkali'. Chose H1285 because 'luminaries of covenant' or 'covenant benefactors' makes sense in a context about titled rulers.
textual_notes: מאו<רים appears to have a damaged character (<). The consonants suggest מאורים from root אור (light), meaning 'luminaries/lights'. However, this may be a Hebrew rendering of a term meaning 'benefactors' (a title given to Hellenistic rulers), which would fit the political context of kings being called by honorific titles.
The phrase מאו<רים ברית could be read as 'luminaries of covenant' (construct chain) or as two separate descriptors. The damaged letter makes certainty impossible.

verses.literal: Kings of nations rule over them and between those who to-them [have] dominion over them are called luminaries of covenant

verses.translation: But [it shall] not be so among you, for the one who is greatest in the household will become like a young servant [or: boy], and the one who is [greatest] will become like the one who serves [or: ministers]

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because 'but/yet' is an adversative conjunction that logically contrasts what follows ('not so among you') with the preceding description of kings ruling.

כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/upright', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'so/thus' pairs with the negation 'not so' to mean 'it will not be this way'.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for/that'. Chose H3588 because it introduces the explanatory clause — 'for the one who is great...'.
שהוא (consonants שהוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because ש + הוא = 'who he [is]', a relative clause construction.

בבית (consonants בבית): Candidates: H1004 'a house/household', H1005 'house', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 because 'in the house/household' fits the context of ranking among a group.

נער (consonants נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/youth/servant', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context contrasts greatness with the lowly status of a youth/servant — the greatest becomes like the youngest.

שמשרת (consonants שמשרת): Candidates: H4958 'a pan', H8334 'to attend/serve as menial or worshipper', H8335 'service'. Chose H8334 because ש + משרת = 'who serves/ministers', which completes the contrast — the greatest becomes like a servant.
textual_notes: The word ]גדול[ appears in brackets in the source text, suggesting a scribal insertion or restoration of a damaged/missing word. This is noted as editorial reconstruction.
בבית could mean 'in the house' or 'in the household/family' — the broader sense of H1004 covers both.

verses.literal: But not it-will-be so from-you for that-one who he [is] great in-the-house will-be as a youth and-that-one who he [is] [great] will-be as that-one who-serves

verses.translation: And I [am] in their midst like one who is serving [or: ministering]

translation_notes: ואני (consonants ואני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'and I' continues the first-person speech from the previous section.
שהוא (consonants שהוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because ש + הוא = 'who he [is]', functioning as a relative pronoun with pronoun.
משרת (consonants משרת): Candidates: H4958 'a pan', H8334 'to attend/serve'. Chose H8334 because the speaker is describing himself as one who serves, consistent with the theme of the previous section.
textual_notes: מי could be interrogative 'who?' or indefinite 'whoever/one who'. In context, the indefinite reading 'one who' makes better sense — 'like one who serves'.

verses.literal: And I in-their-midst as one-who he serves

verses.translation: Yet you [are the ones who] have stood [or: remained firm] with me in my trials [or: testings]

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the adversative 'yet/but' transitions from the teaching about servanthood to an affirmation about the disciples' faithfulness.

לעמוד (consonants לעמוד): Candidates: H5982 'a column/stand/platform'. The root עמד means 'to stand'. The infinitive construct ל + עמוד = 'to stand', which fits 'you [are those who] stand with me'. H5982 as noun 'pillar' is less fitting; the infinitive verbal use makes better sense.
textual_notes: The syntax is compressed. לכם לעמוד could mean 'it is for you to stand' (i.e., you are the ones who stand) or could imply an elliptical verb: '[it belongs] to you to stand with me'. Both produce the same essential meaning.
בנסיונותי has no Strong's candidates provided. The root is נסה (to test/try), and the form is a plural noun with first-person possessive suffix: 'my trials/testings'.

verses.literal: But to-you to-stand with-me in-my-trials

verses.translation: And I [am] preparing [or: establishing] for you a kingdom, just as my Father decreed [or: appointed, covenanted] for me

translation_notes: ואני (consonants ואני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the first-person pronoun continues the speaker's declaration.
מלכות (consonants מלכות): Candidates: H4438 'a rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah'. Chose H4438 because 'kingdom/dominion' is the clear object of 'preparing for you'.

שאבי (consonants שאבי): The relative particle ש + אבי 'my father'. The only candidate listed is H21 'Abi (Hezekiah's mother)' — but in context this is clearly ש + אב with 1cs suffix = 'that my father'. Not the proper noun.
textual_notes: מכין has no Strong's candidates listed. The root is כון (H3559, to be firm/establish/prepare). The participle form מכין = 'preparing/establishing'.

גזרו has no Strong's candidates listed. The root is גזר (H1504, to cut/divide/decree). The form appears to be 3ms perfect with 3ms suffix or possibly 3cp — 'he decreed it' or 'they decreed'. Given the singular subject 'my father', this is likely 3ms perfect: 'he decreed'.

verses.literal: And I preparing for-you a kingdom as my-father decreed for-me

verses.translation: So that you will eat and drink at the table of my kingdom, and you will sit upon thrones [or: elevated seats] and judge the twelve tribes of Israel

translation_notes: בעבור (consonants בעבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'passed/stored grain'. Chose H5668 because 'in order that' introduces the purpose clause — you will eat and drink.
על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top/aloft', H5921 'above/over/upon', H5922 'upon', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'upon' is the natural preposition for sitting on thrones.

מגדל (consonants מגדל): Candidates: H4026 'a tower/rostrum/elevated platform', H1431-H1435 various meanings of גדל. Chose H4026 because in the context of sitting upon elevated structures for judging, 'tower/rostrum/elevated seat' suggests thrones or seats of authority. The word here likely renders a concept of elevated seats of judgment.

עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 '-teen'. Chose H6235 because combined with the preceding 'two' (שנים), this yields 'twelve' — the standard way to express twelve in Hebrew (שנים עשר).
ישראל (consonants ישראל): Candidates: H3478 'Israel', H3479 'Israel'. Chose H3478 as the standard designation.
textual_notes: מגדל is unusual for 'throne'. The typical Hebrew word for throne is כסא. מגדל (H4026) means 'tower/rostrum/elevated platform'. This may be the translator's choice to render a concept of elevated judgment seats. Alternatively, the text may have a different Vorlage or the scribe chose an unusual term.
התיבות has no Strong's candidates listed. תיבה (H8392) means 'box/chest/ark'. In context, 'the seats/boxes' could refer to judgment seats. This is an unusual word choice.
ה<נים appears to have a damaged character. The expected reading is השנים (the two), from שנים (H8147), combining with עשר to form 'twelve'. The damaged letter appears to be ש.
The combination מגדל התיבות is unusual and may represent 'thrones' or 'elevated seats of judgment' — a compound expression not standard in biblical Hebrew.

verses.literal: In-order-that you-will-eat and-you-will-drink at-table-of my-kingdom and-you-will-sit upon thrones the-seats and-you-will-judge the-two ten tribes-of Israel

verses.translation: And YHWH [the LORD] said to Shimon [Simon]: Look! The adversary [the Satan, the accuser] is seeking you [all] in order to sift you through a sieve like wheat

translation_notes: ויהוה (consonants ויהוה): Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH'. Chose H3068 as the standard divine name.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'said' is the verb needed after the subject YHWH.
לשמעון (consonants לשמעון): Candidates: H8095 'Shimon/Simeon', H4583 'an abode', H4584 'Maon'. Chose H8095 because ל + שמעון = 'to Shimon/Simon', the addressee of the speech.

הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold/look!' is the natural interjection introducing a warning.
השטן (consonants השטן): Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'an opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because with the article ה, this is 'the adversary/Satan' — the subject who is seeking them.
מבקש (consonants מבקש): Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek/strive after', H7179 'straw'. Chose H1245 because the participle 'seeking' describes the adversary's active pursuit.
בעבור (consonants בעבור): Candidates: H5668 'in order that/on account of', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because 'in order to' introduces the purpose — to sift them.

בכברה (consonants בכברה): Candidates: H3530 'a measure of distance', H3531 'a sieve', H1262 'to select/feed/render clear'. Chose H3531 because 'a sieve' fits the agricultural imagery of sifting wheat — passing through a sieve produces the clearest physical image.
textual_notes: אתכם is plural 'you all', while the speech is addressed to Shimon. This indicates the adversary is seeking the entire group, not just Shimon alone.
העבירכם has no Strong's candidates listed. The root is עבר (H5674, to pass over/through) in the Hiphil (causative) — 'to cause you to pass through', i.e., to sift you.

verses.translation: But I have prayed on your behalf that your faithfulness [or: faith, steadfastness] will not fail [or: cease], and you, when you turn back [or: are restored], strengthen [or: establish, form] your brothers

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet'. Chose H61 because 'but/yet' provides the adversative contrast — the adversary seeks to sift, but I have prayed.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun continuing the speaker's statement.
לא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
ואתה (consonants ואתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because ו + אתה = 'and you', addressing Shimon directly.
textual_notes: לפעמים is puzzling. פעם (H6471) means 'a time/step/occurrence'. לפעמים could mean 'at times/sometimes'. However, in context this may be rendering a concept like 'when at some point' or 'once' — referring to a future turning point rather than intermittent action.

מתהפך from root הפך (H2015, to turn/overturn) in the Hithpael — 'turning oneself/being turned/returning'. This could mean 'when you turn back' (i.e., repent/are restored) rather than 'at times turning' in a habitual sense.

ותצייר is difficult. The root יצר (H3335) means 'to form/fashion/portray'. The root צור (H6696) means 'to press/bind/besiege'. In context, the expected meaning is 'strengthen/establish your brothers'. The consonants ת-צ-י-י-ר could reflect a form of צייר 'to portray/delineate' or possibly a rendering of a concept like 'establish/set in order'. This word choice is unusual and may reflect the translator's attempt to render a concept of strengthening or confirming.

The overall meaning of the second clause is uncertain: it could read 'and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers' or 'and you at times turn and form/establish your brothers'. The first reading produces a more coherent exhortation.

verses.literal: But I prayed on-your-behalf that-your-faith not will-cease and-you at-times turning and-you-will-portray your-brothers

verses.translation: And he said to him: Master [or: Lord], I [am] ready to go with you into prison and into death. But in you [is] the youth [or: But you treat me as a youth].

translation_notes: והוא (consonants והוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'and he' introduces the subject who responds.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — the verb 'said'.
אדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord/controller', H114 'Addon (Israelite name)'. Chose H113 because 'lord/master' is the natural vocative address.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun.

מוכן (consonants מוכן): The provided candidates are for כן (H3651 'so/upright', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand', H3654 'a gnat'). However, מוכן is a Hophal participle from כון (H3559, 'to be firm/established/prepared'), meaning 'prepared/ready'. This is the correct identification despite not being listed among candidates.
אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet'. Chose H61 — adversative 'but'.

הנער (consonants הנער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/youth/servant', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because 'the youth/boy' connects to the earlier teaching where the greatest becomes like a נער.
textual_notes: The final clause אבל בכם הנער is cryptic. It could mean: (1) 'But among you [I am] the youth' — Shimon affirming he will be the servant; (2) 'But in you [is] the youth' — acknowledging youthful/immature qualities; (3) it may be a fragmentary or corrupt ending. The connection to section 3's teaching about the greatest becoming like a נער suggests this is Shimon relating back to that teaching.
בסוהר has no Strong's candidates listed. סוהר (H5470) means 'prison/dungeon' (from the root סגר, to shut up). This fits 'into prison'.
ובמיתה has no Strong's candidates listed. מיתה is from מות (H4194, death), meaning 'in death'. The form with ב prefix = 'in/into death'.
בכם switches from singular address (עמך 'with you') to plural (בכם 'among you'), which could indicate the speaker now addresses the group, or this may be a textual issue.

verses.literal: And he said to-him lord I ready to-go with-you in-prison and-in-death but in-you the-youth

verses.translation: And Yeshua said, I say to you, Kepha — the rooster will not yet crow, and three times you will be denying [or: disowning] me, and you will not acknowledge me.

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a verb of speech introducing direct discourse.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the speaker is identifying himself as the subject.

אומר (consonants אומר): The only candidate given is H201 'Omar, a grandson of Esau', but this is clearly a participle form of אמר (H559) meaning 'saying/say'. The consonants א-ו-מ-ר form the qal active participle of אמר. Assigning H559.

עדין (consonants עדין): Candidates: H5719 'voluptuous', H5720 'Adin'. Neither fits perfectly; however in post-biblical Hebrew עדין means 'yet/still'. The context (the rooster will not yet call) demands an adverb of time. Reading as 'yet/still'.

כופר (consonants כ-ו-פ-ר): The candidates given only list פר H6499 'bullock', but the full consonants כפר point to the verb כפר meaning 'to deny/cover/disown'. This is a participial form meaning 'denying'. No Strong's number provided directly matches; the root כפר in the sense of denying is contextually necessary.
בי: The candidate H994 'oh that!' is an interjection. Here בי is simply the preposition ב + first person suffix 'in me/against me'.
textual_notes: עדין: In biblical Hebrew this word means 'voluptuous' or is a proper name. The meaning 'yet/still' is post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew, suggesting this text has a later linguistic register.
כופר: The root כפר can mean 'to deny', 'to cover', or 'to atone'. In context 'denying' fits best, but 'covering over' (hiding association) is also possible.
תכירני: From the root נכר (hiphil) 'to recognize/acknowledge'. The combination 'deny me and not recognize me' could be two separate acts or a hendiadys reinforcing one idea.

verses.translation: And he said to them, When I sent you without bag [or: sack] and sandals, did you lack any thing? And they said, No.

translation_notes: להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they'. This is the preposition ל + הם (them). Chose H1992 as the pronoun 'them' with prepositional prefix.
כאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר include H834 'who/which/when'. Chose H834 as a temporal conjunction 'when', producing 'as when I sent you'.
שק (consonants שק): Candidates: H8242 'sacking/bag', H8243 'the leg'. Chose H8242 because 'bag' pairs naturally with 'sandals' as travel provisions.
חסר: Candidates: H2637 'to lack', H2638 'lacking', H2639 'destitution', H2640 'poverty'. Chose H2637 as a verb 'lacked' fitting the interrogative sentence.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 as an interrogative; paired with זה דבר it forms 'which thing?' i.e. 'anything at all?'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as a demonstrative pronoun forming the phrase 'which thing'.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 'thing/matter' as it completes the question about lacking anything.
textual_notes: בזולת: This word is not found in biblical Hebrew Strong's. It is a post-biblical compound (ב + זולת) meaning 'without/apart from', confirming later linguistic register.
אי זה דבר: This could be parsed as 'which thing' (interrogative) or 'any thing at all'. The overall sense is the same — 'did you lack anything?'

verses.translation: And then he said to them, But now, whoever has a bag [or: sack], let him take [it], and also the purse [or: stone], and whoever does not have [one], let him sell his garments and buy a knife [or: blade].

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because 'but/yet' is needed as an adversative conjunction contrasting the previous situation with 'now'.

שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble/white stone', H3426 'there is/are'. The consonants ש+יש form the relative particle ש plus יש 'there is'. Chose H3426 because 'who that has' makes perfect sense contextually.
שק: Candidates: H8242 'sacking/bag', H8243 'leg'. Chose H8242 — 'bag' parallels the travel context from section 2.

האבן: Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'a pair of stones/potter's wheel'. This is puzzling in context — 'take the stone' alongside a bag. This may be a translation artifact for a money-purse or similar object. Chose H68 as the basic reading.
שאין: The relative ש + אין (H369 'non-entity/negative particle'), meaning 'who does not have'.
textual_notes: האבן: 'The stone' is unexpected in a list with bag, garments, and knife. This may represent a Hebrew rendering of an Aramaic or Greek word for 'purse/money-bag' that was confused with or deliberately rendered as אבן. Alternatively, אבן here could be a scribal variant. The parallel tradition has 'purse' (Greek βαλλάντιον). Working solely from consonants, H68 'stone' is the plain reading.

סכין: This word (knife) is post-biblical Hebrew (found in Mishnaic Hebrew), not in the standard Strong's biblical lexicon. The parallel tradition typically has 'sword' (חרב). The text distinctly reads סכין 'knife/blade'.

verses.translation: For I say to you that what is written must be fulfilled [or: carried out] in him, and with the wicked [or: evil ones] he is destined [or: appointed]. For all the things that are concerning me are coming to [their] end [or: fulfillment].

translation_notes: כי (all three occurrences): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction for/that/because'. Chose H3588 in all cases — first as 'for', second as 'that', third as 'for/because'.
ועם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'with the evil ones' describes being counted among them, not 'the people of the evil ones'.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as a pronoun — 'he is appointed'.
שהם: Candidates: H7718 'beryl', H7719 'Shoham', H1992 'they'. The relative ש + הם 'that they'. Chose H1992.
ממני: Candidates: H4507 'Fate/idol', H4508 'Minni (province)', H5204 'lamentation'. None fit; this is simply the preposition מן + first person suffix 'from me/concerning me'.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as the copular pronoun 'they are'.
textual_notes: חוייב and מזומן: These are post-biblical Hebrew forms (Mishnaic/Medieval). חוייב is a passive participle of חייב 'to obligate' and מזומן is a passive participle of זמן 'to appoint/prepare'. Neither appears in the biblical Strong's lexicon.
ממני: Could mean 'from me' (things originating from me) or 'concerning me' (things about me). In context, 'concerning me' fits better — the things written about him are reaching their end.

And they said sovereign look two knives here and he said to them enough
verses.amplified: And they said, "Master [or: Lord], look — [there are] two knives here." And he said to them, "[That is] enough [or: sufficient]."
work: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because this is clearly a pronoun subject preceding the verb 'said' — 'and they said' is the only coherent reading.

אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (proper name)'. Chose H113 because in direct address ('they said ___') a title of respect like 'master/lord' makes sense, whereas Addon as a proper name has no contextual support.

הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Also possible: ה + נה H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because a presentative particle ('look!') naturally introduces the demonstrative statement about what is present — 'look, two knives here.'

שתי: Candidates: H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp in weaving'. Neither fits. However, the consonants שתי are the construct form of H8147 שתים 'two' (feminine construct). In context before a counted noun 'knives,' 'two' is the only coherent reading. The dictionary candidates listed are incomplete; שתי is the standard feminine construct of שנים/שתים.

פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here (this place)'. Chose H6311 because after listing objects ('two knives'), the adverb 'here' completes the spatial demonstration — 'two knives here.' Reading 'mouth' would produce an incoherent image.

והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because the context requires a pronoun subject for the following verb 'said' — 'and he said.'

אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (proper name)'. Chose H559 because in the sequence 'and he ___ to them' a verb of speech is required, and this is standard Biblical Hebrew.
להם: The ל prefix is a preposition 'to,' and הם is H1992 'them.' The candidate H3859 'to burn/rankle' does not fit a context where someone responds verbally. 'To them' is the only coherent reading.

די: Candidates: H1767 'enough/sufficient', H1768 'that (relative conjunction)'. Chose H1767 because as the complete response to a presentation of items, 'enough' or 'sufficient' makes perfect sense — it is a declarative judgment on the quantity presented.
ambiguities: שתי: The Strong's candidates provided (H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp in weaving') do not match the contextual meaning. The consonants שתי are recognized as the feminine construct of the numeral 'two' (related to H8147 שנים/שתים). This is a gap in the provided candidate list rather than a genuine textual ambiguity.

סכינים: No Strong's candidates were provided. The word סכין (plural סכינים) appears in Mishnaic Hebrew and once in the Hebrew Bible (Proverbs 23:2 as מאכלת-type synonym; cf. also Aramaic usage). It means 'knife/knives.' No Strong's number is assigned in the standard list for this word.

די: Could theoretically be read as the relative particle H1768 ('that'), but as a standalone final word in the response, H1767 'enough' is far more natural. If H1768, one would expect a following clause.

translation_notes: המלך: Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429 'Melek', H4430 'a king (Aramaic)', H4431 'advice', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 because 'the king' with the definite article is functioning as a title for the subject (Yeshua).

והתלמידים: This is post-biblical Hebrew (תלמיד = student/disciple, from the root למד). Not in the biblical Strong's lexicon.
כמנהגו: Also post-biblical; מנהג 'custom/practice' is Mishnaic Hebrew.

נסע: H5265 'to pull up tent-pins / start a journey / move away'. This fits perfectly — he moved a distance away from them.
מהם: Preposition מן + הם (H1992). 'From them'.
אבן: Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'pair of stones'. Chose H68 — 'a stone's throw' as a unit of distance.

הברכים: From ברך 'knee' (H1290). The definite article + plural 'the knees'. Could also relate to ברכה 'blessing' but 'knees' fits the physical action of kneeling.

translation_notes: אומר: Only candidate H201 'Omar'. But clearly this is the participle of אמר (H559) 'saying'. Assigning H559.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — conditional 'if' introducing a request.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence addresses God directly: 'if you are willing'.

המות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 title, H4193 'death', H4194 'death'. Chose H4194 because 'the death' as a noun with definite article fits. This is remarkable — the parallel tradition has 'this cup'; this text reads 'this death'.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative 'this' modifying 'the death'.

מעלי: The preposition מעל + first person suffix = 'from upon me'. The candidates for עלי (H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme') are the root עלה/על; here it's simply the compound preposition.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/although', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 as the limiting conjunction 'only/but rather'.

תחפוץ: From חפץ 'to desire/delight in/be willing'. Not in the provided candidates but the root is clear from the consonants.

מלאך: Candidates: H4397 'messenger/angel', H4398 'angel (Aramaic)', H389 'surely'. Chose H4397 as 'messenger/angel of the heavens'.

מחזק: Root חזק. Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/seize/strengthen', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power'. Chose H2388 as a piel participle 'strengthening' — the angel was strengthening him.

translation_notes: מהתפלה (consonants תפלה): Candidates: H8604 'frivolity', H8605 'intercession/supplication/prayer'. Since the context describes rising from an act of praying (section 1 described prayer in distress), H8605 'prayer/supplication' is the obvious fit.
אל: Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/God', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. Following 'came' (ובא), the directional preposition 'to/toward' (H413) is the natural reading.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. 'On account of' fits the context of explaining why the disciples were sleeping; 'stored grain' makes no sense here.

מהלך: Candidates: H4108 'a walking/access', H4109 'a walk/passage/distance', or from root הלך H1980 'to walk'. The word appears before הולך המלך ('going the king'). As a noun H4108/H4109 it could mean 'a procession' or 'a passage.' As a participle from H1980 with מ prefix, it could mean 'from walking.' The noun reading 'procession/approach' fits best with the following phrase about the king coming.
המלך: Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4429-H4432 various. With the article ה, 'the king' (H4428) is the most natural nominal reading.
textual_notes: The phrase מהלך הולך המלך is syntactically ambiguous. It could mean: (1) 'a procession — the king was approaching,' (2) 'walking, the king was going,' or (3) the entire clause could be a separate sentence fragment describing the approach of the arresting party (the king referring to the authority behind the arrest). The relationship between the disciples sleeping and the approaching procession is unclear — whether 'on account of anxiety' modifies only the sleeping or also introduces the approach.

textual_notes: The word לפתוי does not appear in the Strong's candidates provided. הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 same (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. As a pronoun subject before מדבר, H1931 'he' fits naturally.

כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. After 'speaking,' the adverb 'thus/so' (H3651) makes natural sense.

והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold!', H5089 'lamentation'. With ו prefix introducing a sudden scene, H2009 'behold!' is the standard dramatic interjection.

בעבור: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. 'In order that he might kiss him' — H5668 as purpose clause is the clear reading.
לישוע: H3442 and H3443 are essentially the same name. H3442 is the standard entry for Yeshua.
textual_notes: The word מ<נים contains a damaged character (<). It likely reads משנים (from שנים = 'two'), making 'שנים עשר' = 'twelve.' However, the damage makes this partially reconstructed.

היום: H3117 'a day', H3118 'a day (Aramaic)'. H3117 is standard Hebrew. With the article, 'the day' — combined with כל: 'every day.'
ולא: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). H3808 is the standard Hebrew negation.

רק: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. As a conjunction introducing a contrast ('but/only'), H7535 is correct.
ועוז: H5756 'to be strong/strengthen.' The noun form עוז means 'strength/power/might.' In construct with the following word, 'the power/strength of the darkness.'

שלחתם: The candidates listed are for חתם (H2856 'to seal'), but the actual root here is שלח 'to send' with 2mp suffix — שלחתם = 'you sent.' The Strong's candidates appear mismatched; the root is שלח (H7971).
textual_notes: The word הע&רפל contains a damaged character (&). It most likely reads הערפל from ערפל (H6205) meaning 'thick darkness/gloom/dark cloud.' The damage makes this partially reconstructed.

The words 'ועצים' (and trees/counsels), 'שעתנו/שעתינו' (our hour, repeated with variant spelling), 'ועז הערפליי' (and the strong/bold foggy one), and 'היית אשה אתה את' (you were a woman, you) do not form a coherent narrative sequence. This may represent marginal glosses, scribal notes, or textual corruption that has been copied into the main text. The core narrative appears to be: 'And after a little while another time she saw him and said: You too are from them! And Kepha said: Man, I am not!' The remainder may be a corrupted parallel or displaced text.
The apostrophe/quotation mark after אדם is unusual and may represent a scribal notation or paragraph marker.
