verses.literal: And he went out to outside and wept in bitterness

verses.translation: And the people who were holding him mocked him, striking [or: beating] him

translation_notes: והעם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/nation', H5973 'with.' Chose H5971 because the article ה indicates a definite noun 'the people,' not a preposition.

מכים: The candidates listed are for the suffix ים (H3220 'sea' etc.) but this is clearly the hiphil participle plural of נכה H5221 'to strike.' The ים here is the masculine plural participial ending 'ones striking.'
textual_notes: התופשים derives from תפש 'to seize/take hold of' — this is a participial form 'the ones seizing/holding' which is not in the provided candidates but is well-established Hebrew (cf. H8610).

verses.literal: And the people the ones seizing him mocked upon him striking him

verses.translation: And they covered him and struck him in the face [or: on his face], and they asked him, saying, "Prophesy — who is it that struck you?"

translation_notes: נביא (consonants נביא): Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet or inspired man'. In this context the word functions as an imperative command — 'prophesy!' — addressed to the person being struck. Both entries point to the same root meaning. Chose H5030 as the more general entry. Note: the consonants נביא could be parsed as the noun 'prophet' or as an imperative 'prophesy!' The surrounding context (a challenge to identify the striker) strongly supports the imperative reading.

הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because this is a Hebrew clause functioning as a pronoun 'he' in the question 'who is he that struck you.'

שהכה: The ש is the relative particle 'that/who'; הכה is from נכה (to strike/smite). The candidates listed under כה (H3541/H3542 'thus/like this') do not apply here — the root is clearly הכה from נכה meaning 'struck', as the entire context describes physical striking.
textual_notes: נביא could be read as the noun 'prophet' (O prophet! who is he...) or as an imperative 'prophesy!' Both make contextual sense — one mocks his prophetic claim as a title, the other commands him to demonstrate prophetic ability. The imperative reading is slightly favored by the interrogative structure that follows.

verses.literal: And covering him and striking him in [the] face and asking him saying prophesy who is he that struck you

verses.translation: And many curses [or: blasphemies, insults] they spoke against him
verses.literal: And curses many that [they] say against him

verses.translation: And when day came [or: when it became day], the elders of the people and the scribes and the chief priests gathered together and led him into the house of their council [or: their council chamber], saying to him

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher (proper name)', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With the prefixed וכ (and-as/when), H834 is the only candidate that works as a temporal conjunction: 'and when.' All other options would produce incoherent syntax.

העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 (Aramaic people), H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 (Aramaic with). Preceded by זקני ('elders of'), H5971 'the people' is the natural reading — 'elders of the people.'

ושרי (consonants שרי): The listed candidates H8297 'Sarai' and H8298 'Sharay' are proper names that make no sense here. The word is clearly שרי from שר (H8269, 'chief/prince/ruler') in construct plural — 'chiefs of.' The candidates provided do not include H8269 but the consonants שר+י clearly represent the construct plural of שר.

בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 (Aramaic house), H1006 'Bajith (place name)'. With the prefix ב ('in') and followed by עצתם ('their counsel'), H1004 'house' is correct — 'in the house of their counsel' i.e. their council chamber.
textual_notes: עצתם ('their counsel/council') could refer to either the abstract concept of their deliberation or the concrete council body/assembly. Both readings are valid; the phrase 'house of their counsel' likely refers to a council chamber or sanhedrin hall.

verses.literal: And when was made day gathered [the] elders of the people and the scribes and chiefs of the priests and they led him into [the] house of their counsel saying to him

verses.translation: If you [are] the Anointed One [Messiah], tell us! And Yeshua said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe me

translation_notes: אם (first instance): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether/although'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional question — 'if you are the Messiah.'
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you (singular)'. Chose H859 because the syntax requires a pronoun — 'if you [are] Messiah.'

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrub'. Chose H4899 because it functions as a title predicate — 'if you are the Anointed One.'
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context is direct speech — 'Yeshua said.'

להם (consonants להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 with ל prefix — 'to them' — the standard prepositional phrase for indirect object.
אם (second instance): Same analysis as first — H518 'if' introducing a conditional clause.
אומר: H201 'Omar (name)' was the only candidate offered, but this is clearly a qal active participle of אמר (H559) meaning 'I say/am saying.' The proper noun reading makes no sense in context.
textual_notes: אומר — the only Strong's candidate provided was H201 (Omar, a name), but this is transparently the participle of אמר H559 'saying/I say.' I assign it to H559.
תאמינוני has no candidates provided; it is a hiphil imperfect 2mp of אמן with 1cs suffix — 'you will believe me.'

verses.literal: If you [are] Messiah say to us and Yeshua said to them if I say to you you will not believe me

verses.translation: And if I question you, you will not answer me, and you will not release [or: let go of] me

translation_notes: ואם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this continues the conditional pattern from the previous section — 'and if I ask you.'
לא (both instances): Candidates: H3808 'not (absolute negation)', H3809 same in Aramaic. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation particle.
textual_notes: תעזבוני could be from עזב 'to leave/forsake/release' — in this context it could mean 'you will not let me go/release me' or 'you will not leave me alone.' The former fits better with a trial/interrogation setting where the accused might hope for release.
אשאל is 1cs imperfect of שאל (H7592) 'I will ask/question.' No candidates were provided for this inflected form.
תענוני is 2mp imperfect of ענה 'to answer' with 1cs suffix. No candidates were provided.

verses.literal: And if I ask you you will not answer me and not release me

verses.translation: From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power [or: might] of YHWH

translation_notes: בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'crossed/transit — on account of, in order that', H5669 'passed/stored grain'. Chose H5668 because it functions as a temporal/causal adverb — 'on account of this' or 'from this [point forward].'

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this' as the demonstrative object of the preposition. 'On account of a sheep the son of man will sit' is incoherent.
בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 same as H1121. Chose H1121 because 'son of the man/Adam' is a well-known title construction.

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because בן האדם 'son of man/humanity' is the standard construct — it denotes a human being. H121 'Adam' is also possible (son of Adam), but H120 as generic 'man' is the primary reading.
לימין (consonants ימין): Candidates: H3225 'right hand/side', H3226 'Jamin (name)'. Chose H3225 because 'sitting at the right hand of power' describes a position of authority.
כח (consonants כח): H3581 'vigor/force/power' — the only candidate. It describes divine might.
יהוה (consonants יהוה): Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 same. Chose H3068 as the primary entry for the divine name.
textual_notes: בעבור זה could mean 'on account of this' (causal) or 'from this [time onward]' (temporal). Both readings are grammatically valid. The temporal reading ('from now on') fits better with the future tense יהיה 'will be.'
האדם could be H120 'humanity/a human' or H121 'Adam' — 'son of man' vs. 'son of Adam.' Both produce a meaningful title. H120 is the more standard reading for this construct.

verses.literal: On account of this will be [the] son [of] the man sitting at [the] right [of the] power [of] YHWH

verses.translation: And they all said: If so, [then] you [are] the Son of God! And Yeshua said: You [yourselves] are saying that I am he

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — introduces the inferential question 'if so, then you are...'
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because אם כן is a standard idiom meaning 'if so/therefore.'
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 — the pronoun 'you' is required as the subject of the implied copula.
בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben', H1123 same. Chose H1121 — 'son of God' as a title.
האלוה (consonants אלוה): H433 'a deity or the Deity.' With the definite article — 'the God.'
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — Yeshua spoke in response.
שאני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because ש + אני = 'that I' — the relative particle with the first person pronoun. 'That a ship he is' makes no sense.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/self/the same', H1932 same Aramaic, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — the emphatic pronoun 'he' completing the identification: 'that I am he.'
textual_notes: אתם was given only H864 'Etham (a place in the desert)' as a candidate, but this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you (plural).' The Strong's lexicon typically doesn't assign a number to this common pronoun separately; it functions here as subject of the participle אומרים.

The phrase שאני הוא ('that I am he') is an emphatic self-identification. הוא could be read as the existential verb H1933 'to be' rather than the pronoun H1931 'he.' Both produce essentially the same meaning: 'that I am [he]' / 'that I exist [as such].' Chose H1931 as the pronoun reading is more direct.

verses.literal: And they said all of them if so you [are] son [of] the God and Yeshua said you [are the ones] saying that I [am] he

verses.translation: And they said, "Why [or: for what reason] are you still seeking witnesses? Behold — we ourselves have heard it from his [own] mouth!" And all the people [the whole assembly] rose up and led Yeshua [Jesus] to Pilatus [Pilate].

translation_notes: והם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham, a region', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because the waw-prefix + pronoun 'and they' is the natural subject of 'said' in this narrative context; a place name or 'wealth' makes no sense here.

למה (consonants ל-מ-ה): Candidates: H4100 'what? how? why?', H4101 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H4100 because this is Hebrew text and ל + מה = 'for what' = 'why', which fits perfectly as an interrogative introducing the rhetorical question about needing witnesses.

אתם: The only Strong's candidate provided is H864 'Etham, a place in the Desert.' However, אתם is the standard second-person masculine plural pronoun 'you' (not separately listed in Strong's as a standalone lexeme because it is a basic pronoun). Context demands 'you' — the speakers are addressing others directly about their seeking of witnesses. A desert place name is nonsensical here.

עוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/again/further', H5751 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H5750 because the adverbial sense 'still/further' fits the rhetorical question 'why are you still seeking witnesses?' — they already have testimony from his own mouth.

והה: H1929 'ah!' expressing grief. However, in this context והה likely functions as a demonstrative particle 'behold' (variant spelling or interjection drawing attention), introducing the declaration 'we ourselves heard him.' The exclamatory function fits well — it marks the shift from question to emphatic assertion.
כל (consonants כ-ל): Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Chose H3605 as the Hebrew form; 'all the people' is the natural reading.

העם (consonants ע-ם with article ה): Candidates: H5971 'a people/assembly', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 (Aramaic). Chose H5971 because the definite article ה + עם = 'the people/assembly', which is the subject of 'rose up.' A preposition 'with' makes no grammatical sense here.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Yeshua', H3443 (variant). Chose H3442 — the proper name Yeshua (Jesus), the object being led to Pilatus.
textual_notes: The brackets ] [ in the manuscript likely indicate a section break, paragraph division, or a lacuna marker between the two scenes (the declaration about witnesses and the leading of Yeshua to Pilatus). Their exact function is uncertain.

והה could be read as the interjection H1929 'ah!' (expressing grief or exclamation) or as a variant demonstrative particle 'behold/here.' In context the demonstrative-emphatic sense fits better ('behold, we ourselves heard'), but the grief reading ('alas, we ourselves heard') is also possible if the speakers express dismay at what they heard.

אתם is listed only as H864 (Etham, a place name) in the provided candidates, but the consonants are identical to the standard 2nd person masculine plural pronoun. Context unambiguously demands the pronoun.

verses.literal: And they said for-what [are] you asking still [for] witnesses behold we ourselves heard-him from-his-mouth. And rose-up all the people and led Yeshua to Pilatus.
